title: Import-time sys.path prepend can shadow backend modules globally
reasoning: Importing either browser_control_args_schema or schema_types mutates process-global import resolution by inserting frontend/src/main/python at the front of sys.path. Because this happens at module import time and uses index 0, any later import in the backend process can resolve to a same-named module from the sidecar-visible frontend tree before the backend environment or installed packages. That creates order-dependent backend behavior and release hazards that are hard to diagnose, especially in pytest where importing this feature can affect unrelated tests in the same interpreter.
recommendation: Avoid process-global path prepending for the backend import path. Prefer packaging the shared contract as an explicit importable module for both backend and sidecar, or load this specific contract through a bounded import mechanism that does not alter global import precedence. If sys.path mutation is kept temporarily, append rather than prepend and constrain it behind a compatibility note with deletion plan.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and the included files show no guard that verifies imports after this module cannot be shadowed by frontend/src/main/python.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a backend import-order test that imports backend.src.tools.browser.browser_control_args_schema, then verifies a deliberately conflicting module name resolves from the backend or environment path rather than frontend/src/main/python.
minimumFixScope: Change shared_contract_loader.ensure_frontend_python_path and the import strategy used by browser_control_args_schema.py and schema_types.py.
